stem: A new application needs low-latency block storage, and the team wants to avoid paying for capacity that sits unused for months while still being able to grow the volume later without downtime.

choices.text: Provision an io2 volume with the maximum provisioned IOPS from the start
Start the EBS volume at a realistic size and use Elastic Volumes to increase it later as usage grows
Move the workload's data to Amazon EFS instead of EBS
Provision the volume at the largest size the workload could ever need up front

rationale: Starting at a realistic size and using Elastic Volumes to grow the volume later matches actual usage to spend instead of guessing high up front, and Elastic Volumes resizes a live volume with no downtime. Provisioning an io2 volume with maximum IOPS addresses performance, not the unused-capacity cost the team wants to avoid. Moving to Amazon EFS drops the guaranteed low-latency block interface the application needs, because EFS is file storage rather than block storage. Provisioning the largest size the workload could ever need up front is the over-provisioning approach that leaves capacity paid for and unused for months.
